label: HB
reasoning: Both layouts are correct and pass the same test; nothing in the tree measures 'easier to scan' and no earlier decision settles it. Per 'A shown result closes the work; the human's own eye is never the gate on an ordinary delivery,' the Director only shows-and-closes when a command, a test, or a plain read already confirms the outcome — here the observable outcome has no artifact that settles which layout achieves it. This is one of the three reserved cases: a taste call, a trade-off no artifact settles, or a change to the definition of correct. Choosing between a single ranked column and a four-column layout, with no measurement to arbitrate, is a taste call about the experience — so the Director holds and asks rather than closing unilaterally.
